raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Fix multimodal GPU transport lifetime bugs found while investigating #43402. Thanks to @StarDuster for the report and native-stack evidence.

- Release unconsumed features on queued aborts, early rejection, and peer reconstruction failure. Session aborts release the current turn's media without invalidating borrowed history or skipping KV cleanup.
- Keep publisher rollback alive across repeated asyncio cancellation.
- Acknowledge only the current consumer, not its peers; keep unused raw features available for later re-prefill. Match consumer slots to the routed attention-DP group.
- Poll VMM acknowledgements outside the allocator lock and recheck allocation identity before reclaiming. Disable incompatible IPC borrowing for VMM.
- Wait for the producing CUDA stream before VMM publication or CPU fallback, including across the asynchronous publisher's thread boundary.

No pool-size, default-backend, or fixed-HBM-budget change.

## Validation

Remote NVIDIA GB300 development validation at `193aa211b191267f7d75ae70ccf83ab00275469b`:

Current head `7e8e24ec5bd64146e76a2db96102dc97c20dd93c` adds test-fixture corrections only; production source is unchanged. Its nine related CI-entrypoint suites passed all 169 cases in an isolated development checkout with CUDA hidden (exit 0).

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Real CUDA queued-abort A/B | Original main `e8fb52c5`: 1 / 2 / 3 occupied slices after successive cancellations; fixed: 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Source-stream race | Before: received zeros while the producing stream was writing 73; after: received 73 |
| Focused regression suites | 235 passed, including 15 CUDA VMM and 6 CUDA IPC tests; exit 0 |
| CPU-only lifecycle tests | 13 passed with CUDA hidden; exit 0 |
| Two-node, eight-rank FABRIC stress | 10,000 rounds with random 9–35 MiB features and forced CPU fallback; all ranks passed and full pool capacity recovered each round |
| Concurrent fallback smoke | Separate frontend process and 8 consumers, 1 GiB pool, concurrent GPU preprocessing and GEMM/NCCL load: 9,599 dispatches (6,344 VMM / 3,255 CPU fallbacks) in 120 seconds; both nodes exited 0 |
| Real-weight server | Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct, TP8 / two nodes, encoder DP, torchvision, explicit `cuda_vmm`, 8 MiB pool: 64 confirmed queued cancellations followed by 8 successful image requests and healthy generation; pool returned to 0 occupied bytes |

The real server hit pool-full CPU fallback and continued serving. Graphs and radix caching were disabled, with one running request at a time to exercise the waiting queue. This is a correctness regression test, not a performance benchmark.

Regression/server runtime: PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, torchvision 0.29.1+cu130, sglang-kernel 0.4.9, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, transformers 5.19.0. The short FABRIC stress used PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 / sglang-kernel 0.4.7. Driver: 580.159.04. The existing CUDA IPC teardown storage-lifetime warning remains visible.

## Remaining investigation

This fixes the reproduced leak and stream-ordering defects, **not a proven fix for the reported CUDA-driver D2H hang**. A two-hour synthetic baseline soak on original `e8fb52c5` completed 454,724 dispatches (302,413 VMM / 152,311 CPU fallbacks), with all eight consumers passing, both node exits 0, and the full 1 GiB pool free at shutdown. The paired two-hour fixed-source soak at `193aa211` also completed: 453,447 dispatches (301,495 VMM / 151,952 CPU fallbacks), all eight consumers passed, both node and wrapper exits were 0, and the full 1 GiB pool was free at shutdown. Its independent preprocessing loop completed 2,095,671 iterations; maximum observed wrap duration was 0.4287 seconds. Both nodes' logs and exit markers were preserved and SHA-256 verified. Both explicitly synchronize the source stream to isolate the unresolved hang from the separately reproduced stream-ordering bug; this is not a performance comparison.

Neither version reproduced the production hang on driver 580.159.04. This synthetic workload does not replay customer traffic or load full Kimi-K3 weights; the reporter's driver 580.126.20 remains untested. Keep #43402 open for the separate hang investigation.


### Current-head CI limitation

At `7e8e24ec`, lint and the NVIDIA small-GPU job passed, as did 13/14 CPU partitions; Rust artifacts were restored successfully (rebuild skipped). [CPU partition 11](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38025996635/job/114137022062) fails on main-side `self.enterContext` calls introduced by #43442 under Python 3.10. The affected file has the same Git blob in the CI merge and its main parent and is unchanged by this PR. Downstream GPU stages were skipped by that failure gate, so this is **not a fully green CI cycle**. No rerun or unrelated main fix is included here.
